timeline.label: Oct 2023
timeline.event: Rite Aid, then the third-largest US drugstore chain, files for bankruptcy with more than $4 billion of debt and 2,111 stores.
timeline.why: A household name cannot pay its bills.

timeline.label: Sep 2024
timeline.event: It leaves bankruptcy owned by its lenders, after cutting about $2 billion of debt and closing more than 500 stores.
timeline.why: Getting smaller did not fix the business.

timeline.label: Mar 2025
timeline.event: GoodRx finds 48.4 million Americans, about 1 in 7, live in a pharmacy desert, where most people must drive more than 15 minutes to reach their nearest pharmacies.
timeline.why: Access was already thin in many places.

timeline.label: May 2025
timeline.event: Rite Aid files again with about 1,250 stores, this time to close them all and sell its customers' prescription records. CVS plans 271 closures that year, Walgreens 500.

timeline.label: Aug 2025
timeline.event: The last Rite Aid pharmacy in Pennsylvania closes; CVS takes the records of 173 of them there and 42 in New Jersey. Walgreens is taken private by Sycamore Partners.
timeline.why: Weis's main state is hit directly.

timeline.label: Oct 2025
timeline.event: The final 89 Rite Aid stores close after 63 years. CVS says it now serves more than 9 million former Rite Aid patients, from the records of 626 pharmacies in 15 states.
timeline.why: Most patients were handed to a nearby rival.

timeline.event: Weis buys the prescription records of 12 competitor pharmacies (its annual report does not name the sellers).
timeline.why: Weis has started to collect patients, in small numbers.

timeline.label: Jan 2026
timeline.event: Medicare's first negotiated drug prices take effect. Weis says they cut its pharmacy revenue by $18.2 million in the first half of 2026.
timeline.why: A new squeeze on revenue per prescription.

timeline.label: Apr 2026
timeline.event: IQVIA reports Americans used a record 210 billion days of medicine in 2025, up 13% in five years.
